subtopic: Net Asset Value vs. Market Price
source_evidence: Investors buy and sell ETF shares on national stock exchanges and at market prices that may or may not be the same as the NAV of the shares.
answer: An ETF’s net asset value (NAV) reflects the underlying value of its holdings, while its market price is the price investors trade its shares for on an exchange. The two prices may differ. If the market price is above NAV, buyers pay more than the underlying value; if it is below NAV, they pay less. Sellers may likewise receive more or less than NAV when they sell.
